GROUND LEASE

THIS GROUND LEASE (this "Lease") is made as of June 1, 2026 between Ashcombe Land Trust, a Maryland statutory trust ("Landlord"), and Verdant Row Development LLC, a Maryland limited liability company ("Tenant").

RECITALS

A. Landlord owns the unimproved parcel of approximately 4.7 acres at the northeast corner of Talbot Avenue and Ninth Street, Silver Spring, Montgomery County, Maryland, legally described on Exhibit A (the "Land").

B. Tenant intends to construct and operate a mixed-use building containing approximately 214 residential units and 11,000 square feet of ground-floor retail on the Land (the "Project").

C. Landlord is willing to lease the Land to Tenant on the terms set out below.

1. DEMISE AND TERM

1.1 Demise. Landlord leases the Land to Tenant, and Tenant leases the Land from Landlord, on the terms of this Lease.

1.2 Term. The term begins on the Commencement Date and continues for ninety-nine (99) years, expiring on May 31, 2125, unless terminated earlier as this Lease provides (the "Term"). This is a ground lease, and Tenant's estate is a leasehold estate in the Land only.

1.3 Commencement Date. The Commencement Date is the later of July 1, 2026 and the date Landlord delivers possession of the Land free of occupants.

2. RENT

2.1 Base Rent. Tenant shall pay annual Base Rent of $840,000, payable in equal monthly installments in advance on the first day of each month, without abatement, deduction, offset, or counterclaim.

2.2 Escalation. Base Rent increases by ten percent (10%) on the fifth anniversary of the Commencement Date and on each fifth anniversary thereafter, and is reset to fair market ground rent on the fiftieth anniversary, determined by three-appraiser arbitration if the parties cannot agree.

2.3 Net Lease. This Lease is absolutely net to Landlord. Tenant shall pay all taxes, assessments, insurance premiums, utilities, and every other cost relating to the Land, the Improvements, and the Project, and Landlord shall bear no cost of any kind.

3. IMPROVEMENTS

3.1 Right to Construct. Tenant may construct, alter, and demolish improvements on the Land (the "Improvements") at its sole cost, in accordance with plans Landlord approves, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. Landlord shall cooperate, at no cost to Landlord, in obtaining permits and entitlements, and shall execute applications and plats Tenant reasonably requests.

3.2 Ownership During the Term. During the Term, Tenant owns the Improvements and is entitled to all depreciation and tax benefits attributable to them. The Improvements are the property of Tenant and are not part of Landlord's fee estate until the Term ends.

3.3 Reversion. On expiration or earlier termination of this Lease, title to the Improvements vests in Landlord automatically, without payment, free and clear of all liens and encumbrances other than those Landlord created, and Tenant shall deliver the Improvements in good condition and repair, ordinary wear and tear excepted.

3.4 No Obligation to Rebuild at End of Term. Tenant has no obligation to construct or restore Improvements during the final five (5) years of the Term, and may instead maintain the Land in a safe and lawful condition.

4. LEASEHOLD MORTGAGE

4.1 Right to Encumber. Tenant may, without Landlord's consent, mortgage or otherwise encumber its leasehold estate and the Improvements to an Institutional Lender. Tenant may not encumber Landlord's fee estate.

4.2 Notice and Cure. Landlord shall deliver to each leasehold mortgagee of which it has notice a copy of every notice of default it gives Tenant, and no notice is effective as to the mortgagee until delivered. Each leasehold mortgagee has an additional thirty (30) days after Tenant's cure period to cure a monetary default, and an additional sixty (60) days to cure a non-monetary default, plus such further time as it reasonably requires to obtain possession or complete a foreclosure, provided it keeps Rent current.

4.3 New Lease. If this Lease terminates because of Tenant's default or a bankruptcy rejection, Landlord shall, on written request from the most senior leasehold mortgagee delivered within sixty (60) days after the termination, enter into a new lease of the Land with that mortgagee or its designee for the remainder of the Term, on the same terms and with the same priority, provided the mortgagee cures all monetary defaults and pays Landlord's reasonable costs.

4.4 No Merger. No merger of the leasehold and fee estates occurs by reason of either estate being acquired by the same person, and no such merger occurs without the written consent of each leasehold mortgagee.

4.5 Amendment and Surrender. No amendment, cancellation, or voluntary surrender of this Lease is effective without the written consent of each leasehold mortgagee.

5. USE, COMPLIANCE, AND MAINTENANCE

5.1 Use. Tenant may use the Land and the Improvements for any lawful purpose consistent with applicable zoning, and shall not commit waste.

5.2 Compliance. Tenant shall comply, at its cost, with all applicable law affecting the Land, the Improvements, or Tenant's use, including all environmental law and the Fair Housing Act.

5.3 Maintenance. Tenant shall maintain, repair, and replace the Land and the Improvements at its sole cost and keep them in good order and condition. Landlord has no maintenance, repair, or replacement obligation.

6. INSURANCE AND CASUALTY

6.1 Insurance. Tenant shall maintain builder's risk insurance during construction, and thereafter special-form property insurance on the Improvements for full replacement cost, commercial general liability insurance of at least $10,000,000 per occurrence, and rent-loss insurance covering twenty-four (24) months, each naming Landlord and each leasehold mortgagee as their interests appear.

6.2 Casualty. If the Improvements are damaged, Tenant shall restore them at its cost, and Rent does not abate. This Lease does not terminate on account of casualty, and insurance proceeds shall be applied to restoration under a customary construction disbursement agreement with the leasehold mortgagee.

7. CONDEMNATION

7.1 Total Taking. If the whole of the Land is taken, this Lease terminates, and the award shall be apportioned between Landlord and Tenant according to the then-values of the fee estate encumbered by this Lease and the leasehold estate including the Improvements, determined by appraisal.

7.2 Partial Taking. If less than the whole is taken, this Lease continues, Base Rent is reduced in proportion to the value taken, and Tenant shall restore the remainder using its share of the award.

8. ASSIGNMENT AND TRANSFER

8.1 By Tenant. Tenant may assign this Lease, without Landlord's consent, to a leasehold mortgagee, to a purchaser at foreclosure, or to any transferee that assumes this Lease in writing and has a net worth of at least $25,000,000. Any other assignment requires Landlord's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld. Tenant may sublease any portion of the Improvements without consent.

8.2 By Landlord. Landlord may convey the fee estate subject to this Lease, provided the transferee assumes Landlord's obligations in writing.

9. DEFAULT AND REMEDIES

9.1 Tenant Default. It is an Event of Default if Tenant fails to pay Rent within ten (10) days after written notice, or fails to perform any other obligation within sixty (60) days after written notice, or, if the cure reasonably requires longer, fails to begin within that period and prosecute the cure diligently.

9.2 Landlord's Remedies. On an Event of Default, and subject in every case to Section 4, Landlord may terminate this Lease and recover possession and damages permitted by Maryland law.

9.3 Landlord Default. If Landlord fails to perform an obligation within thirty (30) days after written notice, Tenant may perform it and offset the reasonable cost against Rent, or pursue any remedy at law or in equity.

10. ESTOPPEL AND RECORDING

10.1 Estoppel Certificates. Each party shall deliver an estoppel certificate to the other, or to any lender or transferee, within fifteen (15) days after request.

10.2 Memorandum. The parties shall execute and record a memorandum of this Lease promptly after the Commencement Date.

11. GENERAL

11.1 Governing Law; Venue. This Lease is governed by the laws of the State of Maryland. Any action arising out of this Lease shall be brought in the Circuit Court for Montgomery County, Maryland.

11.2 Notices. All notices shall be in writing and delivered by hand, by nationally recognized overnight courier, or by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the addresses stated beneath the signatures, and to each leasehold mortgagee of which the sender has notice.

11.3 Entire Agreement; Amendment. This Lease is the entire agreement between the parties and may be amended only in a writing signed by both, subject to Section 4.5.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Lease as of the date first written above.
